## Linear models with covariates

**Design matrix ($X$)** — the matrix a model formula builds: one row per sample,
one column per coefficient. The model is $\mathbf{y} = X\boldsymbol\beta + \boldsymbol\varepsilon$.
See [Design matrices for covariates](covariates/lec.qmd).

**Dummy (indicator) variable** — a 0/1 column for one level of a factor.
A factor with $k$ levels gets $k-1$ dummies.

**Reference level** — the factor level without a dummy column; it is absorbed
into the intercept, and every other level's coefficient is a difference from it.
R picks the alphabetically first level unless you use `relevel()`.

**Full column rank** — the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, so $\boldsymbol\beta$
has a unique solution. Linearly dependent columns (the dummy-variable trap, a batch
identical to the treatment, an empty cell, more columns than samples) give infinitely
many solutions: `lm` reports `NA`, DESeq2 says the model matrix is "not full rank".

**Adjustment** — adding a covariate as a column of $X$; the other coefficients are
then read "holding that covariate constant".

**Confounder** — a variable that affects both the predictor of interest and the
outcome. Leaving it out biases the effect. *Perfect* confounding (e.g. all treated
samples in one batch) cannot be fixed in the analysis, only in the experimental design.
See [Confounding & Simpson's paradox](confounding/lec.qmd).

**Simpson's paradox** — an effect that has one sign in the pooled data and the
opposite sign within every group, because the groups are unevenly mixed.

**Mediator / collider** — a variable on the causal path from treatment to
outcome (mediator), or one caused by both (collider). Adjusting for either can
create bias rather than remove it.

**Interaction** — a product column in $X$ that lets the effect of one predictor
depend on the level of another.

**Log2 fold change** — the scale on which DESeq2 reports coefficients: 1 means
doubled, −1 halved. See [Design matrices in R](covariates-r/lec.qmd).
